#!/bin/sh
# Every tracked .mlpl file opens with a module-purpose comment and is in
# canonical format per the adjacent sw-MLPL formatter (or $MLPL_FMT, absolute).
set -eu

repo_dir=$(CDPATH= cd -- "$(dirname -- "$0")/.." && pwd)
files=$(find "$repo_dir" -type f -name '*.mlpl' \
    -not -path "$repo_dir/.git/*" -not -path "$repo_dir/.agentrail/*" \
    -not -path "$repo_dir/tmp/*" -not -path "$repo_dir/pages/*" | sort)

if [ -z "$files" ]; then
    echo "MLPL style: no source files yet"
    exit 0
fi

formatter=${MLPL_FMT:-"$repo_dir/../sw-mlpl/scripts/mlpl-fmt.sh"}
case "$formatter" in
    /*) ;;
    *) echo "MLPL_FMT must be an absolute path: $formatter" >&2; exit 1 ;;
esac
if [ ! -x "$formatter" ]; then
    echo "missing canonical formatter: $formatter" >&2
    exit 1
fi

for file in $files; do
    first=$(sed -n '/^[[:space:]]*$/d; p; q' "$file")
    case "$first" in
        \#*) ;;
        *) echo "missing module-purpose comment: ${file#"$repo_dir/"}" >&2; exit 1 ;;
    esac
    "$formatter" --check "$file"
done
echo "PASS MLPL style"

#!/bin/sh
# .gitignore is sane: runtime caches are ignored, reviewed outputs are not,
# and nothing ignored is tracked.
set -eu

repo_root=$(CDPATH= cd -- "$(dirname -- "$0")/.." && pwd)
status=0

# Paths that must be ignored (reg-rs runtime caches, scratch output).
for probe in tests/reg/x.tdb tests/reg/x.tdb.lock tmp/x scratch.tmp; do
    if ! git -C "$repo_root" check-ignore -q "$probe"; then
        echo "not ignored but should be: $probe" >&2
        status=1
    fi
done

# Paths that must NOT be ignored (reviewed baselines, fixtures, the site).
for probe in tests/reg/x.rgt tests/reg/x.out tests/reg/x.err fixtures/x.json pages/index.html; do
    if git -C "$repo_root" check-ignore -q "$probe"; then
        echo "ignored but must be tracked: $probe" >&2
        status=1
    fi
done

# Nothing tracked may match an ignore rule.
tracked=$(git -C "$repo_root" ls-files -ci --exclude-standard)
if [ -n "$tracked" ]; then
    echo "tracked files match .gitignore:" >&2
    echo "$tracked" >&2
    status=1
fi

[ "$status" -eq 0 ] || exit 1
echo "PASS gitignore"

entries.description:
Use a mouse and keyboard to interact with a web browser, and take screenshots. If you don't have a valid tab ID, use tabs_context_mcp first to get available tabs.
* Whenever you intend to click on an element like an icon, you should consult a screenshot to determine the coordinates of the element before moving the cursor.
* If you tried clicking on a program or link but it failed to load, even after waiting, try adjusting your click location so that the tip of the cursor visually falls on the element that you want to click.
* Make sure to click any buttons, links, icons, etc with the cursor tip in the center of the element. Don't click boxes on their edges unless asked.

action.description:
The action to perform:
* `left_click`: Click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `right_click`: Click the right mouse button at the specified coordinates to open context menus.
* `double_click`: Double-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `triple_click`: Triple-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `type`: Type a string of text.
* `screenshot`: Take a screenshot of the screen.
* `wait`: Wait for a specified number of seconds.
* `scroll`: Scroll up, down, left, or right at the specified coordinates.
* `key`: Press a specific keyboard key.
* `left_click_drag`: Drag from start_coordinate to coordinate.
* `zoom`: Take a screenshot of a specific region for closer inspection.
* `scroll_to`: Scroll an element into view using its element reference ID from read_page or find tools.
* `hover`: Move the mouse cursor to the specified coordinates or element without clicking. Useful for revealing tooltips, dropdown menus, or triggering hover states.

coordinate.description: (x, y): The x (pixels from the left edge) and y (pixels from the top edge) coordinates. Required for `left_click`, `right_click`, `double_click`, `triple_click`, and `scroll`. For `left_click_drag`, this is the end position.

text.description: The text to type (for `type` action) or the key(s) to press (for `key` action). For `key` action: Provide space-separated keys (e.g., "Backspace Backspace Delete"). Supports keyboard shortcuts using the platform's modifier key (use "cmd" on Mac, "ctrl" on Windows/Linux, e.g., "cmd+a" or "ctrl+a" for select all). Page zoom shortcuts (e.g. "cmd+=", "ctrl+-", "cmd+0") are not supported and will return an error - use the `zoom` action to magnify a region of the page instead.

duration.description: The number of seconds to wait. Required for `wait`. Maximum 10 seconds.

scroll_direction.description: The direction to scroll. Required for `scroll`.

scroll_amount.description: The number of scroll wheel ticks. Optional for `scroll`, defaults to 3.

region.description: (x0, y0, x1, y1): The rectangular region to capture for `zoom`. Coordinates define a rectangle from top-left (x0, y0) to bottom-right (x1, y1) in pixels from the viewport origin. Required for `zoom` action. Useful for inspecting small UI elements like icons, buttons, or text.

scale.description: For `screenshot` and `zoom` only. Scale factor in [0.1, 1] for the returned image; 1 (default) uses the full image token budget, 0.5 returns an image at half the width and height (~quarter of the tokens). Coordinates are ALWAYS in the full-resolution coordinate frame (reported with every scaled screenshot), never in the scaled image's own pixels. Requires a Claude in Chrome extension version that supports scale; older extensions return the full-size image.

repeat.description: Number of times to repeat the key sequence. Only applicable for `key` action. Must be a positive integer between 1 and 100. Default is 1. Useful for navigation tasks like pressing arrow keys multiple times.

ref.description: Element reference ID from read_page or find tools (e.g., "ref_1", "ref_2"). Required for `scroll_to` action. Can be used as alternative to `coordinate` for click actions.

modifiers.description: Modifier keys for click actions. Supports: "ctrl", "shift", "alt", "cmd" (or "meta"), "win" (or "windows"). Can be combined with "+" (e.g., "ctrl+shift", "cmd+alt"). Optional.

tabId.description: Tab ID to execute the action on. Must be a tab in the current group. Use tabs_context_mcp first if you don't have a valid tab ID.

save_to_disk.description: For screenshot/zoom actions: save the image to disk so it can be attached to a message for the user. Returns the saved path in the tool result. Only set this when you intend to share the image — screenshots you're just looking at don't need saving.

--- capture-site head
#!/bin/sh
# Capture the stones from the served page with headless Chrome: one still of
# every stone at an angle, mid-way through its time axis, and one animated
# WebP of every Visual face across its time axis. Needs the page served at
# http://127.0.0.1:8765/ (just serve-site), Google Chrome, ImageMagick and
# img2webp/cwebp. Writes captures/. usage: scripts/capture-site
set -eu

repo_root=$(CDPATH= cd -- "$(dirname -- "$0")/.." && pwd)
cd "$repo_root"
chrome=${CHROME:-"/Applications/Google Chrome.app/Contents/MacOS/Google Chrome"}
base=${SITE:-http://127.0.0.1:8765/}
mkdir -p captures tmp/cap

shot() {
    "$chrome" --headless=new --disable-gpu --hide-scrollbars --window-size=1280,1100 \
        --virtual-time-budget=6000 --screenshot="$1" "$base?$2" >/dev/null 2>&1
}

# stone  still-step  step-count
while read -r stone mid count; do
    [ -n "$stone" ] || continue
    shot "tmp/cap/$stone.png" "stone=$stone&yaw=-32&epoch=$mid"
    magick "tmp/cap/$stone.png" -crop 1000x620+140+230 +repage -resize 900x "captures/$stone-stone.png"
    rm -f tmp/cap/f_*.png
    step=$(( (count + 11) / 12 ))
    t=0; i=0; frames=""
    while [ "$t" -lt "$count" ]; do
        name=$(printf 'tmp/cap/f_%02d.png' "$i")
        shot "$name" "stone=$stone&read=visual&epoch=$t"
        magick "$name" -crop 960x560+160+170 +repage -resize 720x "$name"
        frames="$frames -d 500 $name"
        t=$((t + step)); i=$((i + 1))
    done
    # shellcheck disable=SC2086
    img2webp -loop 0 -lossy -q 70 $frames -o "captures/$stone-visual.webp" >/dev/null 2>&1
    echo "captured $stone ($i frames)"
done <<STONES
one-neuron 12 31
dot-product 3 6
--- stones test

12:  while lt(k, 7) {

content.text:
Step 029 is done and pushed: two commits on `main`, the stone commit and the saga record.

**What landed: the image-normalization stone.** The Math face reads z[h,w,c] = (x[h,w,c] − μ[c]) / σ[c] with a second line for the index space, h ∈ Fin(4), w ∈ Fin(4), c ∈ Fin(3). The M face keeps the feature stone's line unchanged, Z ← (X − Μ) ÷ Σ, and adds the shapes X : Tuple[4,4,3] and Μ Σ : Tuple[3]. The docs on both faces say the tuples are broadcast by the index map (h, w, c) ↦ c and never materialized to the image's shape. The image is a 4×4×3 ramp plus a bright spot computed by MLPL, and z comes from trailing-axis broadcasting, which a test checks against three explicit loops. Time is the pixel, sixteen steps row by row. The Visual face has three channel grids with the current pixel outlined, μ and σ drawn once with a leader from the current pixel, three output grids filling in, and an index-projection panel. It sits after softmax and before the CNN in the dropdown. Three baselines, two tests, README tour entry and status. The gate is green with 64 tests and 28 baselines. I checked the Visual, Math and turned stone with headless Chrome screenshots and widened the grids once so three-digit cells read.

**Your question about pane 2 callouts.** I could not reproduce it: the Chrome extension was not connected in this session, so I read the code instead, and I did not find a cause I can stand behind. What I can rule out: the M face's SVG, docs and line tags are identical in structure to the one-neuron stone's, so it is not the sigmoid record. The hover path is the same for all three faces, and a text face always gets at least the nearest line's callout, so a truly dead face means either the pointer events are not reaching that face's section or the anchor projection is producing off-screen positions for it. Two things worth checking when you next see it, with the console open:

- Whether `document.elementFromPoint` over the dead area returns something inside the M face section or another element.
- Whether the callout root exists but its boxes have huge or NaN `left`/`top` values, which would mean the projection for that face's transform is wrong.

I suggest inserting a step for this so the fix is tracked. I have not done that, since it changes the plan's order.

**One loose end for you.** `docs/research2.txt` is still untracked, and both the README and `docs/plan.md` link to it, so those links are broken on GitHub. Committing it is your call since it is your research notes.

Next step in the saga is 030, the attention stone.
